clinician.trajectory_summary: A 14-year-old girl with a known history of primary hypoparathyroidism, diagnosed at age 9 based on hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, and low serum PTH. At age 14, she was hospitalized for severe hypercalcemia with symptoms including dyspnea, generalized weakness, polydipsia, nausea, and tachycardia, which resolved after intensive fluid therapy, loop diuretics, and temporary withdrawal of vitamin D and calcium. Around the same time, mild nonprogressive bilateral nephrocalcinosis was detected by renal ultrasound, along with persistent hypercalciuria and a normal eGFR. Laboratory tests at age 14 continued to show low sPTH, low 25-OH-vitamin D, low alkaline phosphatase, hyperphosphatemia, and decreased total and ionized calcium. Ultrasound also revealed a duplex left kidney with mild dilatation.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented at age 9 with hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, and low serum parathyroid hormone (sPTH), consistent with primary hypoparathyroidism.
Mild nephrocalcinosis was detected by renal ultrasound in September 2015 (age 14).

At age 14, laboratory tests showed low sPTH, low 25-OH-vitamin D, low alkaline phosphatase, hyperphosphatemia, and clearly decreased levels of total and ionized calcium, along with persistent hypercalciuria and normal eGFR.

In January 2015 (age 14), the patient was hospitalized due to severe hypercalcemia with dyspnea, generalized weakness, polydipsia, nausea, and tachycardia, which resolved after intensive fluid therapy, loop diuretics, and temporary withdrawal of vitamin D and calcium.
Ultrasound examination also revealed a duplex left kidney with a mild dilatation of the upper-pole collecting system.
